files.item: The poster for The Liberty Tree, an event from the Election Special 2010.
files.notes: The Liberty Tree, by Robb Johnson and Leon Rosselson, is a collection of words and music depicting the life of Thomas Paine. The poster incorporates the James Gillray (1756–1815) cartoon 'Fashion before Ease;—or,—A good Constitution sacrificed for a Fantastick Form'. Paine, who wrote The Rights of Man, started his working life as a corset maker. The Election Special was the spring event series of 2010.

This poster was used to advertise an event discussing the Chartist movement, featuring Dorothy Thompson (1923–2011). Chartism was a 19th Century working-class movement which campaigned for parliamentary reform. The Election Special was the spring event series of 2010.
The 1970s: Life Before Thatcher was the autumn event series of 2010. The poster is adapted from a photograph of the police attempting to hold back a picket line at the Grunwich strike in 1977.

files.item: Political Football: Meanings and Mystery at the World Cup 2010 flyer.
files.notes: This flyer advertised a one-off event with David Goldblatt marking the 2010 World Cup. The photograph is of Russian keeper Lev Yashin saving a free-kick in the 1966 World Cup semi-final against West Germany at Goodison park. The photograph on the back fo the flyer is of Tom Finney playing for England against Belgium in the 1954 World Cup.

files.notes: The skeleton is from Osteographia, or the Anatomy of Bones by William Cheselden (1688–1752), 1733.

This is a flyer that was used to advertise BRHG itself, rather than a particular event. The character of Death is from 'Death on the Barricade', part of The Dance of Death by Alfred Rethel (1816–1859), 1849. The BRHG logo is adapted from a 'gallows ticket' for the execution of Jonathan Wild (1682 or 1683–1725), engraved by Thomas Cook (c.1744–1818).
